This command triggers the ReplicaSet associated with our Deployment to create a new replica of the Pod with the same YAML manifest.

By executing this command, we are essentially asking Kubernetes to:
1. Recreate the pod "my-k8s-app".
2. Fetch the latest configuration for this pod from its respective Deployment object.
3. Ensure that the new pod is healthy and ready to serve requests again.

In simpler terms, we're telling Kubernetes to try creating our application (my-k8s-app) pod once more by reusing its original configuration. This might solve the issue if it was a one-time problem like an intermittent network connection or unauthorized access when pulling the image.

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1

metadata:
  name: this-pod-will-crash
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      containers:
```

1. Check if the image exists in a publicly accessible Docker registry or in a private one to which your cluster has proper credentials. If it's a private registry, make sure that your cluster has the necessary authentication details (username, password, token) to access it.
2. Verify that the image name, tag, and repository are correct. Make sure there is no typo or mistake in any of them. For example: my-image:v1, docker.mycompany.com/my-namespace/my-image:v1
3. Inspect your deployment configuration to ensure it has the correct image pull policy. By default, Kubernetes uses "IfNotPresent" pull policy which means that if the image already exists on the node, it will use the local copy; otherwise, it will try to pull it from the registry. You can change this policy using the `imagePullPolicy` field in your deployment YAML:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-k8s-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-k8s-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-k8s-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: my-container
        image: docker.mycompany.com/my-namespace/my-image:v1
        imagePullPolicy: Always # or Never, if you want to use a local copy of the image if it exists on the node
```

4. Check if there are any network issues preventing your cluster nodes from accessing the Docker registry. If your cluster is using a proxy, make sure that the image registry is whitelisted and accessible through the proxy.

```sh
kubectl describe pod my-k8s-app-57fd566645-7v2sx
```

